findings.title: Path traversal in shared attachment download
findings.explanation: name comes straight from the query string and is joined into the path without secure_name(), so an anonymous holder of any share link can request ?name=../../notes.db and read the whole database (password hashes, every note) or any other readable file. Use self.attachments.read(note.id, name).

findings.title: Anyone can create a share link for someone else's note
findings.explanation: create_share looks the note up with get_by_id and only checks deletion, never note.owner_id == user.id. Any logged-in user can iterate ids and publish other users' notes. Use self.owned_note(user, note_id).

findings.title: Share expiry check is inverted
findings.explanation: The link is rejected while expires_at > now, i.e. while it is still valid, and accepted once it has expired, so fresh links 404 and expired links work forever. The condition must be expires_at <= now.

findings.title: get_by_id returns soft-deleted notes; owned_note now uses it
findings.explanation: The old owned_note used get(), which filters deleted_at IS NULL. get_by_id has no such filter, so after DELETE the note is still readable via GET /notes/<id>, its attachments download, PATCH crashes with AttributeError, and share links keep serving it, contradicting the README.

findings.title: Share token written to the audit log
findings.explanation: The share token is a bearer credential; recording token=... in the operator-readable audit table lets anyone with audit access open the shared note, which the README explicitly forbids. Log only the note id (or a token hash).
